--- title: "Post-Transplant Cyclophosphamide Meta-Analysis" subtitle: "Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of PTCy vs alternative GVHD prophylaxis platforms" date: 2026-05-29 --- ## Abstract ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Background.** Post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) has become widely adopted for GVHD prophylaxis in allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation, yet comprehensive quantitative evidence synthesis across survival, GVHD, and infection outcomes — and across comparator regimens — has been lacking. **Methods.** We conducted a Bayesian random-effects meta-analysis of 251 studies (14 RCTs) comparing PTCy to (1) CNI+MTX/MMF-based regimens (Comparison 1) and (2) ATG-based regimens (Comparison 2). Primary outcomes included overall survival (OS), non-relapse mortality (NRM), acute GVHD grade II–IV, CMV reactivation, bloodstream infection (BSI), and invasive fungal infection (IFI). Steroid-mediation models (M2) tested whether GVHD-driven steroid exposure confounded observed effects. **Results.** PTCy was associated with improved OS (C1: OR 0.79 [0.73–0.85]; C2: OR 0.82 [0.71–0.94]), reduced aGVHD (C1: OR 0.67; C2: OR 0.58), and reduced relapse-related mortality (C1: OR 0.83; C2: OR 0.79) across both comparators. CMV reactivation was increased vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.26 [1.07–1.47]) but near-null vs ATG (OR 0.98 [0.78–1.24]), consistent with a T-cell depletion depth gradient. BK virus (C1: OR 2.48; C2: OR 2.44) and BSI (C1: OR 1.87) were elevated regardless of comparator. Within-PTCy regimen variants (C3, k = 4–7) showed no significant differences across outcomes. **Conclusions.** PTCy provides consistent survival, GVHD, and anti-relapse advantages regardless of comparator. CMV risk follows a T-cell depletion depth gradient rather than reflecting a PTCy-specific property. BK virus and BSI elevations are comparator-independent. GRADE certainty is LOW for OS and aGVHD, VERY LOW for other outcomes. ::: --- ## Executive Summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} exec_list <- list( or_os, or_m2_os, or_nrm, or_m2_nrm, or_agvhd, or_cmv, or_m2_cmv, or_bsi, or_ifi, or_c2_os, or_c2_m2_os, or_c2_nrm, or_c2_agvhd, or_c2_cmv, or_c2_m2_cmv ) # Add new outcomes if available if (!is.null(post_rrm)) exec_list <- c(exec_list, list(or_rrm)) if (!is.null(post_c2_rrm)) exec_list <- c(exec_list, list(or_c2_rrm)) if (!is.null(post_bk)) exec_list <- c(exec_list, list(or_bk)) if (!is.null(post_c2_bk)) exec_list <- c(exec_list, list(or_c2_bk)) outcome_levels <- rev(c("OS", "NRM", "RRM", "aGVHD II\u2013IV", "CMV", "BK Virus", "BSI", "IFI")) pd <- do.call(rbind, exec_list) |> as_tibble() |> mutate( outcome = factor(outcome, levels = outcome_levels), comparison = factor(comparison, levels = c("C1: PTCy vs CNI+MTX", "C2: PTCy vs ATG")), label = sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", or, lo, hi), y_num = as.numeric(outcome), y_pos = y_num + ifelse(model == "M2", -0.15, 0.15) ) n_outcomes <- length(unique(pd$outcome)) ggplot(pd, aes(x = or, y = y_pos, shape = model, fill = model)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = jama_grey, linewidth = 0.4) + geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, colour = model), size = 0.5, linewidth = 0.5) + geom_text(aes(x = hi, label = label), hjust = -0.05, size = 2.5, colour = jama_black, show.legend = FALSE, nudge_y = 0.25) + scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.5, 2, 3)) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq_len(n_outcomes), labels = outcome_levels[seq_len(n_outcomes)]) + scale_shape_manual(values = c("M1" = 16, "M2" = 21), labels = c("M1 (Direct)", "M2 (Steroid-adjusted)")) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = jama_steel), labels = c("M1 (Direct)", "M2 (Steroid-adjusted)")) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("M1" = jama_navy, "M2" = "white"), labels = c("M1 (Direct)", "M2 (Steroid-adjusted)")) + facet_wrap(~ comparison) + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.25, 5.5)) + labs(x = "Odds Ratio (log scale)", y = NULL, shape = NULL, colour = NULL, fill = NULL, caption = "Bayesian random-effects models (binomial family, brms). Post-Block-9 update.") + theme_jama(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Bayesian meta-analysis — PTCy effect across outcomes and comparators. Filled circles represent direct-effect models (M1); open circles represent steroid-adjusted models (M2). The dashed vertical line marks OR = 1 (no effect). OR < 1 favours PTCy for mortality, GVHD, and IFI outcomes.](index_files/figure-html/fig-exec-summary-1.svg){#fig-exec-summary} ::: ::: ### Key Findings ::: {.key-finding} **1. Survival and GVHD benefit.** PTCy was associated with reduced overall mortality (C1 OR 0.79; C2 OR 0.82) and acute GVHD (C1 OR 0.67; C2 OR 0.58) in both comparisons. The effects were consistent in direction across comparators. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **2. Anti-relapse benefit preserved.** Relapse-related mortality was reduced in both comparisons (C1 OR 0.83; C2 OR 0.79), with no steroid mediation. This supports preserved graft-versus-leukaemia activity and helps explain the residual OS benefit after steroid adjustment. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **3. CMV depletion gradient.** PTCy increased CMV reactivation vs CNI+MTX/MMF (OR 1.26) but showed a near-null effect vs ATG (OR 0.98). Rather than a binary reversal, the evidence now supports a T-cell depletion depth gradient: CNI < PTCy ≈ ATG. ::: ::: {.key-finding} **4. BK virus and BSI elevated.** BK virus reactivation (C1 OR 2.48; C2 OR 2.44) and BSI (C1 OR 1.87) were elevated regardless of comparator. BK virus has a dual mechanism (urothelial toxicity + T-cell depletion). ::: ::: {.key-finding} **5. Within-PTCy variants equivalent.** Comparison 3 found no significant differences across PTCy regimen variants for OS, NRM, aGVHD, or cGVHD, suggesting that the PTCy component dominates the regimen effect. ::: ### Summary of Evidence ::: {#tbl-exec-summary .cell tbl-cap='Summary of primary outcomes across both comparisons.'} ```{.r .cell-code} # Build dynamically from posterior draws get_k <- or_c2_os$p_dir * 100)), list("NRM", "C1", fmt_or(or_nrm$or, or_nrm$lo, or_nrm$hi), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_nrm$p_dir * 100)), list("aGVHD II\u2013IV", "C1", fmt_or(or_agvhd$or, or_agvhd$lo, or_agvhd$hi), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_agvhd$p_dir * 100)), list("aGVHD II\u2013IV", "C2", fmt_or(or_c2_agvhd$or, or_c2_agvhd$lo, or_c2_agvhd$hi), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_c2_agvhd$p_dir * sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_ifi$p_dir * 100)) ) if (!is.null(post_rrm)) { summary_rows <- c(summary_rows, list( list("RRM", "C1", fmt_or(or_rrm$or, or_rrm$lo, or_rrm$hi), sprintf("P(<1) = %.0f%%", or_c2_rrm$p_dir * 100)) )) } if (!is.null(post_bk)) { summary_rows <- c(summary_rows, list( list("BK Virus", "C1", fmt_or(or_bk$or, or_bk$lo, or_bk$hi), sprintf("P(>1) = %.0f%%", or_bk$p_dir * 100)) ````` ::: ::: ### Mechanistic Framework The findings resolve into a unified framework built on three separable consequences of PTCy: 1. **GVHD suppression pathway** (intended): PTCy → reduced aGVHD → less steroid exposure → lower NRM → improved OS. The OS benefit is partially mediated by steroid reduction, with a substantial residual component attributable to anti-relapse activity (RRM benefit). 2. **GVL preservation pathway** (intended): PTCy → reduced relapse-related mortality (C1 OR 0.84; C2 OR 0.79), with no steroid mediation. This is the first meta-analytic demonstration of the GVL preservation benefit and explains the residual OS advantage after steroid adjustment. 3. **T-cell lymphodepletion pathway** (unintended): PTCy depletes CMV-specific and bacterial-specific T cells during engraftment. The CMV depletion gradient across comparisons (CNI < PTCy ≈ ATG) confirms this is a depth-of-depletion effect. BK virus reactivation has a dual mechanism (urothelial toxicity + T-cell depletion), explaining why its effect size (OR ~2.5) exceeds CMV and BSI. ```{mermaid} %%| fig-width: 8 %%| label: fig-mechanism %%| fig-cap: "Dual-pathway mechanistic framework for PTCy effects." flowchart LR PTCy --> A["↓ Alloreactive\nT cells"] PTCy --> B["↓ Pathogen-specific\nT cells"] PTCy --> U["Urothelial\ntoxicity"] A --> C["↓ aGVHD\nOR 0.58–0.67"] A --> R["↓ RRM\nOR 0.79–0.84"] C --> D["↓ Steroid\nexposure"] D --> E["↓ NRM\n(mediation uncertain)"] D --> F["↓ OS\n(partially mediated)"] R --> F B --> G["↑ CMV vs CNI\nOR ~1.3"] B --> H["≈ CMV vs ATG\nOR ~0.9"] B --> I["↑ BSI\nOR ~1.9"] B --> J["↑ BK Virus"] U --> J["↑ BK Virus\nOR ~2.5"] style A fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style B fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style U fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style C fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style R fill:#a3c1d4,stroke:#2b5c8a,color:#1a2a3a style G fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style H fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style I fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a style J fill:#d4d8dc,stroke:#6b7d8d,color:#1a2a3a ``` --- *Navigate to individual pages using the menu above for detailed results, model diagnostics, sensitivity analyses, GRADE assessments, and risk-of-bias evaluation.* ::: {.callout-tip} ## Post-Block-9 Update (2026-06-01) This analysis includes 251 studies (525 arms, 14 RCTs) extracted through Block 9, an expansion from the original 220-study baseline.
